meta.description: A Living Standard that defines Sparklingstadt, an aspiring web engineer who likes Node.js, web standards, TypeScript, Go, Kotlin, and Apple's Human Interface Guidelines.

s1.title: Abstract
s1.body: This document defines Sparklingstadt, an aspiring web engineer. Sparklingstadt prefers implementations that follow the specifications and respect each user's environment, writes mostly TypeScript, and has a strong interest in Go and Kotlin. Sparklingstadt enjoys reading Apple's Human Interface Guidelines [HIG] and is learning Chinese, Russian, and Czech.
s2.title: Status of this document
s2.body: This document is a Living Standard. It is updated as new projects ship and as learning progresses. Earlier versions are available in the GitHub commit history.
s2.note: Without JavaScript, this document is shown in English. Language and theme preferences are stored only in your browser.
s3.title: Conformance
s3.intro: The key words MUST and SHOULD in this section are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119]. When writing code, Sparklingstadt follows these requirements.
s3.r1: Whatever can be built with web standards must be built with web standards.
s3.r2: The color scheme, motion, and text size that each user has chosen must be respected.
s3.r4: The main content should remain readable without JavaScript.
s4.intro: Skills and interests are represented by the following type.
s4.note: TypeScript is the main language. Go and Kotlin are being learned; the projects in §5 show how far each one goes.
s5.title: Projects
s5.intro: My projects range from language learning and typing practice to e-commerce and food journals. This section brings a few of those public projects together.
s6.title: Environment
s6.macos: Sparklingstadt likes macOS for being stylish and practical at the same time.
s6.linux: Building a rice on Arch Linux with Hyprland led Sparklingstadt to an interest in Linux itself.
s6.note: A rice is a customized desktop, built by editing configuration files such as hyprland.conf.
s7.title: Natural languages
s7.intro: Apart from programming languages, Sparklingstadt is learning the following natural languages.
s7.note: Zhuelog (§5.1) is a tool made for studying Chinese.
s8.title: Contact
s8.body: Feedback on this document is welcome on GitHub.
s9.title: Design proposals
s9.body: Design proposals for this site are published as working mocks: an Apple HIG version, a multilingual version, and versions that switch between macOS, Arch Linux + Hyprland, Material 3, and HarmonyOS.
s9.note: The mocks are in Japanese only and are not indexed by search engines.
